name: PyYAML
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/PyYAML/6.0.3/json (License: MIT in the wheel METADATA; LICENSE file in the sdist and wheel)
input_api: yaml.load(local YAML bytes, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader), the pure-Python safe loader; the decoded str and a local binary stream give the same tree
documentation_evidence: The PyYAML documentation says yaml.load accepts a byte string, a Unicode string, an open binary file object or an open text file object, and documents SafeLoader as the loader that resolves only standard YAML tags. CSafeLoader is documented separately as the LibYAML-based loader.
scope: One YAML 1.2 document from local bytes as a typed tree on the two schema-neutral valid controls. PyYAML applies YAML 1.1 implicit resolvers; the controls avoid every scalar whose type differs between YAML 1.1 and the 1.2 core schema. No tags, merge keys, multi-document streams or malformed input were tested.
family: PyYAML pure-Python loader (yaml/scanner.py, parser.py, composer.py, SafeConstructor, YAML 1.1 Resolver); not the libyaml CSafeLoader route
family_note: Pure-Python PyYAML: yaml/reader.py decodes the bytes, scanner.py and parser.py build the event stream, composer.py builds nodes, SafeConstructor builds dict/list/scalars and resolver.py applies the YAML 1.1 implicit resolvers. The pinned manylinux wheel also ships the _yaml C extension (libyaml), but yaml.SafeLoader does not use it; yaml.CSafeLoader is the separate libyaml-family route, selected as its own path (projects/yaml/python/pyyaml_csafeloader). ruamel.yaml derives from this code; yamlcore wraps it (selected wrapper path); oyaml only re-exports it on Python 3.7+.
shared_families: PyYAML pure-Python loader lineage (ruamel.yaml derived from it; yamlcore wraps it; oyaml re-exports it)

popularity.metric: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors
popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads include transitive installs and dump-only use; they do not measure YAML parsing.

name: PyYAML CSafeLoader (libyaml)
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/PyYAML/6.0.3/json (License: MIT in PKG-INFO; LICENSE in the sdist); libyaml 0.2.5 License file (MIT) pinned by SHA-256
input_api: yaml.load(local YAML bytes, Loader=yaml.CSafeLoader); the decoded str and a local binary stream give the same tree
documentation_evidence: The PyYAML documentation describes the LibYAML bindings: CLoader/CSafeLoader are used as yaml.load(input, Loader=CSafeLoader) and parse with LibYAML; yaml.load accepts byte strings, Unicode strings and open files.
scope: One YAML 1.2 document from local bytes as a typed tree on the two schema-neutral valid controls. libyaml scans and parses; PyYAML's SafeConstructor applies YAML 1.1 implicit resolvers, which the controls make schema-neutral. No tags, merge keys, multi-document streams or malformed input were tested.
family: libyaml 0.2.5 through PyYAML's _yaml C extension (CParser), with PyYAML's Python SafeConstructor and YAML 1.1 Resolver; not the pure-Python SafeLoader route
family_note: Same PyPI package and release as the selected PyYAML path but a separate route and parser family, as the YAML cell protocol requires: CSafeLoader subclasses _yaml.CParser, which feeds the input to libyaml's yaml_parser_parse (reader.c, scanner.c, parser.c) and composes nodes in Cython; only SafeConstructor and the Resolver are Python. The pure-Python yaml/scanner.py and parser.py never run on this route. The image builds libyaml 0.2.5 (the release embedded in the official 6.0.3 wheels) from the pinned tarball and links it statically into _yaml. It shares the libyaml family with projects/yaml/c/libyaml and the libyaml-derived C in ruamel.yaml.clib.
shared_families: libyaml (C libyaml cell path; ruamel.yaml.clib vendors an older libyaml snapshot)
PyYAML package (same distribution as the pure-Python SafeLoader path)

popularity.metric: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors
popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads of the PyYAML distribution, recorded unchanged for both the pure SafeLoader and the CSafeLoader routes; PyPI does not split downloads by loader, so the figure does not measure CSafeLoader use or YAML parsing.

name: ruamel.yaml
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/ruamel.yaml/0.19.1/json (License: MIT in the wheel METADATA; LICENSE file in the sdist and wheel)
input_api: ruamel.yaml.YAML(typ='safe', pure=True).load(local YAML bytes); the decoded str and a local binary stream give the same tree
documentation_evidence: The ruamel.yaml basic-usage documentation shows YAML(typ='safe') loading from a string or stream and documents pure=True to force the pure-Python implementation instead of the C-based loader.
scope: One YAML 1.2 document from local bytes as a typed tree on the two schema-neutral valid controls. ruamel.yaml applies the YAML 1.2 resolver by default. No tags, merge keys, multi-document streams or malformed input were tested.
family: ruamel.yaml pure-Python loader (PyYAML-derived Reader/Scanner/Parser/Composer, SafeConstructor, YAML 1.2 VersionedResolver); not the ruamel.yaml.clib(z) C route
family_note: ruamel.yaml began as a PyYAML fork and keeps a PyYAML-derived Reader/Scanner/Parser/Composer, separately maintained with YAML 1.2 support. typ='safe', pure=True selects ruamel/yaml/parser.Parser with the pure Reader and Scanner, SafeConstructor and the YAML 1.2 VersionedResolver; no C loader is installed (ruamel.yaml.clib, the C route, is selected as its own path; clibz is a separate lead). srsly.yaml_loads wraps this exact route (selected wrapper path); strictyaml wraps this package.
shared_families: PyYAML-derived pure-Python loader lineage (with the selected PyYAML path)

popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads include transitive installs and dump-only use; they do not measure YAML parsing.

name: ruamel.yaml.clib
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/ruamel.yaml.clib/0.2.15/json (License: MIT in PKG-INFO; LICENSE in the sdist)
input_api: ruamel.yaml.YAML(typ='safe').load(local YAML bytes) with ruamel.yaml.clib installed (CParser); the decoded str and a local binary stream give the same tree
documentation_evidence: The ruamel.yaml basic-usage documentation shows YAML(typ='safe') loading from a string or stream and says typ='safe' uses the C based loader when available (pure=True forces the Python one); the ruamel.yaml 0.19.1 README says to install ruamel.yaml.clib to get the C loader and main.py imports CParser from _ruamel_yaml.
scope: One YAML 1.2 document from local bytes as a typed tree on the two schema-neutral valid controls. ruamel.yaml.clib scans, parses and composes; ruamel.yaml applies the YAML 1.2 resolver. No tags, merge keys, multi-document streams or malformed input were tested.
family: libyaml-derived C reader/scanner/parser vendored in ruamel.yaml.clib (older libyaml snapshot) with the Cython _ruamel_yaml CParser, under ruamel.yaml's SafeConstructor and YAML 1.2 VersionedResolver; not the pure-Python ruamel.yaml route
family_note: A separate PyPI package with its own metric and C sources, not an empty compatibility distribution: the sdist vendors api.c, reader.c, scanner.c, parser.c and loader.c derived from libyaml. Compared with libyaml 0.2.5, 2,001 of its 2,082 distinct non-test lines longer than 25 characters also occur in libyaml (reader.c byte-identical; scanner.c, parser.c, api.c and loader.c differ, e.g. the older yaml_parser_scan_tag_uri signature), so it is a libyaml-family snapshot shared with the PyYAML CSafeLoader path and the C libyaml path. ruamel.yaml 0.19.1 selects CParser for typ='safe' unless pure=True; constructor and resolver stay in Python. Coverage counts the libyaml-derived C only (profile-list.txt leaves the Cython binding uninstrumented).
shared_families: libyaml (C libyaml cell path; PyYAML CSafeLoader path)
ruamel.yaml Python front end (selected ruamel.yaml path)

name: srsly
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/srsly/3.0.1/json (License: MIT in the wheel METADATA; LICENSE in the sdist)
input_api: srsly.yaml_loads(local YAML text as str); the raw bytes and a local binary stream, passed unchanged to ruamel.yaml, give the same tree
documentation_evidence: The srsly 3.0.1 README (PyPI long description) documents srsly.yaml_loads(data) with data as "str / IO" returning the deserialized content, and lists ruamel.yaml as the YAML library it uses.
scope: One YAML 1.2 document from local text as a typed tree on the two schema-neutral valid controls, through ruamel.yaml's YAML 1.2 resolver. No tags, merge keys, multi-document streams or malformed input were tested.
family: Wrapper: srsly.yaml_loads over ruamel.yaml 0.19.1 YAML(typ='safe', pure=True), the pure-Python ruamel.yaml loader; not an independent parser
family_note: Clearly a wrapper (Parsel/minidom precedent), not a mapping layer: srsly.yaml_loads builds srsly._yaml_api.CustomYaml(), a ruamel.yaml YAML subclass with defaults typ='safe', pure=True, and returns CustomYaml().load(data); ruamel.yaml reads, scans, parses, composes and constructs. srsly 3.x depends on the released ruamel.yaml (the older vendored srsly.ruamel_yaml copy is gone), so this path runs the same ruamel.yaml code as the selected ruamel.yaml path. On both controls srsly executes the same lines; the control differential is in ruamel.yaml scanner.py/parser.py.

name: yamlcore
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/yamlcore/0.1.1/json (License: MIT License in the wheel METADATA; LICENSE in the sdist)
input_api: yaml.load(local YAML bytes, Loader=yamlcore.CoreLoader); the decoded str and a local binary stream give the same tree
documentation_evidence: The yamlcore 0.1.1 README (PyPI long description) shows d = yaml.load(y, Loader=CoreLoader) for YAML 1.2 core-schema loading on top of the PyYAML BaseLoader, and names CCoreLoader as the libyaml variant.
scope: One YAML 1.2 document from local bytes as a typed tree on the two schema-neutral valid controls, with yamlcore's YAML 1.2 core-schema resolver. No tags, merge keys, multi-document streams or malformed input were tested.
family: yamlcore CoreLoader: PyYAML 6.0.3 pure-Python BaseLoader (Reader/Scanner/Parser/Composer) with yamlcore's YAML 1.2 core-schema resolver and constructors; not CCoreLoader (libyaml)
family_note: Wrapper over the PyYAML pure-Python loader (shared with the selected PyYAML path), not a fork: CoreLoader = yaml.BaseLoader + yamlcore CommonConstructor + CommonResolver. During a load its own code supplies the YAML 1.2 core implicit-resolver patterns that PyYAML's resolver applies to each plain scalar and runs its own mapping, int, float, bool and null constructors; it changes typing semantics (1.2 core instead of PyYAML's 1.1 resolvers) but does no scanning or parsing. The control differential is in PyYAML scanner.py/parser.py.

popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads; they do not measure YAML parsing.
